text:
The pedestrian's statement is hearsay if offered to prove the man failed to signal, but it likely qualifies as an excited utterance or present sense impression because it was blurted out immediately after the accident while the pedestrian was still under the stress of observing it—so it is probably admissible. The statement is an emotional reaction to a startling event made close in time, satisfying the excited utterance exception, and the declarant's unavailability does not bar it. On balance, the statement is admissible.

CONFIDENCE: 65
